archetype.name: Play-In Team (frontcourt-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo frontcourt is among the league's best. A thin, poorly graded backcourt and wing rotation caps it somewhere between the play-in and a low playoff seed.

report.headline: A wall at the rim, a sieve on the perimeter, and a 2-4 hole
report.take:
Miami is 2-4 and 19th on the site, but this is not a team without a spine. The frontcourt grades an A, and it runs through Giannis Antetokounmpo, first among 85 power forwards on the site: a 33.3 USG % at a 61.6 TS % with a 7.4 BPM. Bam Adebayo and Bobby Portis both sit in the top quarter of their tabs. The problem is everyone else. The backcourt grades C- and the wings a D, and Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson are each running a BPM around -4.

That split shows up on defense almost perfectly. Opponents are barely getting to the rim, and when they do they don't finish. Opp Rim Rate ranks 4th and Opp Rim FG % ranks 3rd, both far better than last season's marks. But they're shooting 40.5% from three, 29th in the league, and guards are feasting. Shooting guards have put up 56.17 points-rebounds-assists a game against Miami, 29th relative to their own averages, and take a bigger share of the points than the league norm. The result is a 117.3 DRtg, 24th, for a franchise whose defense ranked 5th or 9th in four of the last five seasons.

The numbers hide two things in opposite directions. First, the three-point defense is mostly noise. A 5.6-point gap to the league in Opp 3P % over six games is the kind of number that shrinks, and a defense this good at the rim should settle closer to average overall. Second, the record is honest. W vs Pt Diff is 0, the margin implies exactly 2 wins, and the full-season pace is 27 wins. Miami hasn't been unlucky in close games; it has simply been outscored. The fix has to come from the defense normalizing, not from coin flips turning.

The direction is encouraging. After a four-game losing streak to open, the Heat won at Atlanta and hung 145 on Indiana. Over the last five games they're +6 with a point differential 4.37 a game better than their season mark. The offense is efficient enough at 114.2 ORtg (13th), with a low 12.7 TOV % (5th), to win games once the opponent shooting cools.

strengths.title: Elite rim protection and paint denial
strengths.body: Opponents take only 24.2% of their shots at the rim, 4th fewest, and convert just 61.2% there, 3rd best. Both are well ahead of last season's 29.9% rate and 65.0% finishing. With Antetokounmpo and Adebayo each logging the most minutes on the roster, this is structural rather than a fluke and should hold.

strengths.title: Giannis as a one-man engine
strengths.body: Antetokounmpo leads the team with 169 points and 74 rebounds on a 61.6 TS % while using a third of the possessions, and he ranks 1st on his position's tab. His -13.4 On-Off is a six-game lineup quirk next to a 7.4 BPM, not a real signal. He is the reason the frontcourt grades an A.

strengths.title: Efficient, careful, fast offense
strengths.body: Miami scores 118.33 a game (9th) at a 103.6 pace with a 54.5 eFG % (12th), and it rarely gives the ball away: TOV % ranks 5th. That ball security has been a franchise trait across the last five seasons, so it is likely to last.

concerns.title: Guards are carving up the perimeter
concerns.body: Shooting guards rank 29th in production allowed relative to their own averages. Point guards are scoring 7.67 points a game above their norms. Shooting guards also take 29.5% of the points against Miami, versus 25.2% league-wide. Some of this is hot shooting, but the C- backcourt and D wings grades suggest the point-of-attack defense is a real weakness, not just bad luck.

concerns.title: Opponent three-point shooting at 40.5%
concerns.body: Opp 3P % ranks 29th, 5.6 points worse than the league average, and it's the main reason Opp eFG % sits 27th despite the rim numbers. Over six games, much of that is variance that should fade. If it doesn't, the perimeter closeouts are the culprit, and the defense stays bottom-ten.

concerns.title: Wing minutes going to negatives
concerns.body: Wiggins and Thompson take most of the wing minutes, and both carry BPMs around -4 and On-Off marks near -18. Thompson's 19 threes give the offense spacing, but these two minutes-heavy wings are where the lineups bleed.

trend.note: A four-game losing streak to open gave way to two straight wins. Over the last five games Miami is +6, with its point differential 4.37 a game better than the season mark.

weekAhead.headline: Four-game West Coast trip: two traps, two chances
weekAhead.body:
All four games are on the road, with a Clippers-Warriors back-to-back in the middle. The Lakers are the toughest test: 5-2, 6th on the site, and 1st in both eFG % and TS %. Their point guards drive 34.8% of their scoring, which points straight at Miami's leakiest spot. Golden State shoots 40.0% from three (2nd) on a high 3PA Rate, a dangerous matchup for a defense allowing 40.5% from deep.

The other two games are there to be taken. The Clippers are 1-5, turn it over more than anyone, and let opponents finish 71.8% at the rim. That is a ripe target for Antetokounmpo. Sacramento is 0-6 with a -18.4 Net Rtg, dead last, and the league's worst rim defense. A 2-2 trip is par; 3-1 would put Miami back to .500 and validate the recent turn.

keyMatchups.title: Lakers' guards against Miami's perimeter
keyMatchups.body: The Lakers lean on their point guards for far more of their scoring than the league norm and shoot a league-best eFG %. Miami's guards have been the weak link defensively. This is the game where the perimeter problem costs the most.

keyMatchups.title: Warriors' threes vs. Miami's closeouts
keyMatchups.body: Golden State ranks 2nd in 3P % and 5th in 3PA Rate, and it owns the league's best ORB %. Its D- frontcourt and 29th-ranked rim defense give Antetokounmpo and Adebayo room inside. It is the second half of a back-to-back, though.

keyMatchups.title: Two soft rim defenses to attack
keyMatchups.body: The Clippers allow 71.8% at the rim and lead the league in turnovers. The Kings allow 75.5% at the rim and give power forwards 4.06 points over their norms. These are the games for Miami's frontcourt to pile up efficient points.

weekAhead.watch: Whether opponents' three-point shooting cools against the Lakers and Warriors. It decides whether this defense is bottom-ten or merely slow out of the gate.

restOfSeason.body:
The 27-win pace is the floor case, not the forecast. The rim protection and ball security look real, and the 40.5% opponent three-point shooting does not. If the defense drifts back toward the middle of the pack, a DRtg in the 113-116 range, the Net Rtg turns positive, and Miami looks like last year's 43-39 team again. That points to a 36-44 win range, squarely in play-in territory in a weak Southeast where nobody is above .500.

What won't fix itself is the guard and wing talent. With the backcourt at C- and the wings at D, Miami's ceiling depends on Antetokounmpo staying at a near-MVP level. Larsson's efficient play (66.6 TS %, positive On-Off) is the best internal hope for better perimeter minutes. Expect opponent three-point shooting to settle around 35.5-37.5%, not stay above 40.
swingFactors: Better production from the guard and wing rotation

confidence.note: Six games; the shooting splits are noisy.
